newsitem.title: USA: Dollar ends higher on signs of Japanese weakness.
newsitem.headline: Dollar ends higher on signs of Japanese weakness.

text.p: The dollar rose against most major currencies Wednesday amid fresh signs of economic weakness in Japan and renewed calls for a stronger dollar from European officials.

The Bank of Japan reported its quarterly tankan business confidence index improved in November, but only to minus three from minus seven in August, sparking investors to sell Japanese yen for dollars. The news suggested Japan's economy is still too weak to tolerate higher interest rates.
"The tankan report was not terrible, but the market had been short dollars against expectations of a slightly better report," said Ben Strauss, currency trader at Bank Julius Baer & Co.

The dollar rose to 113.30 yen from 112.50 late Tuesday and also climbed to 1.5270 German marks from 1.5245. Against the French franc, the dollar rose in late trading before closing nearly flat at 5.1725 from 5.1720.

The dollar gained versus European currencies after French Prime Minister Alain Juppe told an audience in Paris that he thought the dollar was undervalued. Juppe also said he would ask other leaders of the Group of Seven industrialised nations to discuss the dollar's weakness.
Juppe's comments helped boost the dollar against the mark and the French franc.
"Certainly it's his 'undervalued' statement in line with yesterday's French comment that's doing this," said Kevin Lawrie, global manager of foreign exchange at Mellon Bank N.A.

Paul Marchelli, a member of the Bank of France monetary policy council, said Tuesday he believed most European currencies were overvalued against the dollar and that the French franc was overvalued by about 10 percent.
The dollar had less success against the British pound, which climbed on renewed talk of higher interest rates in Britain.

Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke told a press conference in London he was prepared to raise interest rates if necessary to counter inflationary pressures as the British economy continues to expand.
"The comments gave sterling a little bit of firmness," said Strauss. "It had had a pretty good sell-off the last couple of days and now it's bouncing."
Trading wound down early Wednesday ahead Thursday closure of U.S. financial markets for the Thanksgiving holiday. Foreign exchange trading will resume in the United States on Friday.
In other trading, the dollar rose to 1.2910 Swiss francs from 1.2903. The dollar also climbed to Canadian $1.3461 from C$1.3427.
